region: Trumansburg · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Bet the Farm is a small, woman-owned winery founded by Nancy Tisch, a scientist who came to Cornell from Rhode Island for postdoctoral research. She began in Aurora with a wine and local-food shop on Main Street; because New York law required a shop selling both wine and food to make its own wine, she made her first vintage in 2006 with guidance from neighbouring Finger Lakes winemakers. The winery now has a quiet tasting room on Krums Corners Road outside Trumansburg, near Cayuga Lake.

Gamay Noir, the grape of Beaujolais, is a house speciality: Bet the Farm makes five different wines from it, and the 2024 Gamay Noir was released as the fifth. The winery grows red varieties on a six-acre estate vineyard and also buys fruit from other Finger Lakes growers. The cool lake climate keeps Gamay light, bright and low in alcohol. It is 11.7% alcohol and fully dry.
